clue.text: Silence everyone! That's indicative of the future

parts.note: 'Sh!' is the call for silence
everyone means all

explanation.surface: Someone calls a room to order before making a grand pronouncement about what is to come.
explanation.definitionFit: This auxiliary verb marks the future tense, as in 'we will go' or its formal first-person form.

clue.text: Quite right for commercial traveller to retire

parts.note: being for something means being pro it

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the word for the traveller is read backwards

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative who travels on business

explanation.surface: A salesman's decision to stop working is judged entirely sensible.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper conduct is correct and fitting, exactly what 'quite right' describes.

clue.text: A type of suit or suite

definitions.text: A type of suit or suite

parts.words: A type of suit or suite
parts.note: a style of clothing in two matching items, or furniture or bathroom fittings sold as a matched pair

explanation.definitionFit: Two matching pieces make up both a jacket-and-trousers outfit and a small matched furniture set.

clue.text: Lynn appears in time, as is typical

indicators.note: appearing in something means being placed inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: an age is a long period of time
Vera Lynn was the British wartime singer known as the Forces' Sweetheart

explanation.surface: A remark that a certain singer shows up in time, as she usually does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lynn' is a surname, but the solver needs the famous singer's first name; 'appears in' is the container signal, and 'as is' merely links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something typical is ordinary and representative, just as a middling, run-of-the-mill result is.

clue.text: What marriage bureaux do to find a wife

definitions.meaning: dating agencies assist people in getting together: they help (people) meet
an old word for a spouse who is a suitable helper

explanation.surface: A man signs up with a matchmaking agency in hope of finding a bride.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic term for a spouse or partner, derived from Genesis; the first sense splits it into two everyday words.

clue.text: Study text in draft

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn by heart
a script is the written text of a play or speech

explanation.surface: A student pores over a piece of writing that is still at the rough stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draft' looks like a rough version of the text, but it is the verb meaning to call up for military service.
explanation.definitionFit: To draft someone, in the military sense, is to enlist them compulsorily into the armed forces.

clue.text: Brief greeting from radio band

parts.note: brief means short
a wave of the hand is a greeting

explanation.surface: A quick hello is heard coming over the airwaves.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a range of radio frequencies used for long-distance broadcasting.

clue.text: Leading man acquires new bird

parts.note: the hero is the main male character in a story

explanation.surface: The star of the show takes on a fresh feathered co-star.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-legged wading bird of rivers and marshes.

clue.text: In general, I don't like the beach

indicators.note: 'In' tells us the letters lie inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone confesses a general dislike of seaside holidays.
explanation.definitionFit: A public open-air swimming area or bathing beach, often at a resort.

clue.text: Insecticide used by smart daily

parts.note: fly is informal for sharp or smart
a daily is a newspaper published every day

explanation.surface: A bug-killer is being used by a clever newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Insecticide' here means something that kills insects; a sticky strip does that, so the definition is fair if loose.
explanation.definitionFit: A sticky strip of coated sheet that traps and kills household insects.

clue.text: Duty to deliver one thousand letters

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
the Roman numeral M is a thousand
post is mail, the letters delivered

explanation.surface: A postman's task is to deliver a thousand letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An impost is a tax or levy, as is a customs duty.

clue.text: Breton means to make cheese

parts.note: Br. is a dictionary abbreviation used for Breton
i.e. (Latin id est, 'that is') introduces what a statement means

explanation.surface: A man from Brittany sets about making cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft French cheese with a white rind, named after a region east of Paris.

clue.text: Subject needing analysis from all angles

definitions.text: Subject needing analysis from all angles

parts.words: Subject needing analysis from all angles
parts.note: a school subject whose work is literally measuring angles, besides needing a thorough look

explanation.definitionFit: This branch of mathematics deals with shapes, lines and the angles between them.

clue.text: Vessel that always carries a warhead

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it within, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: e'er is the poetic shortening of ever, meaning always
the head of the word war is its first letter, W

explanation.surface: A missile is described that always bears an explosive tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'warhead' reads as a bomb, but it means the first letter of 'war'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large jug or pitcher, a vessel for water.

clue.text: Visor enables one to maintain dignity

definitions.meaning: a visor literally protects the face
something that lets a person avoid humiliation

explanation.surface: A piece of headgear lets its wearer keep their self-respect.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a guard for the face, and idiomatically a move that spares someone embarrassment.

clue.text: Naval complement was exultant

definitions.meaning: the sailors who man a ship
one past tense of crow, to boast or exult

explanation.surface: A ship's company celebrated loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's company of sailors; also a past tense of crow, meaning boasted triumphantly.

clue.text: 22 disposed to go mad

indicators.note: disposed means arranged, so the letters are set out in a new order

parts.note: refers to the answer at 22 across, a woman's name

explanation.surface: Clue 22 is inclined to lose her temper.
explanation.walkthrough: '22' points to another answer in the grid; its four letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To rave is to talk wildly as if insane.

clue.text: Elixir from an adept in Pennsylvania

indicators.note: 'in' places the middle pieces within the abbreviation

parts.note: PA is the postal abbreviation for Pennsylvania
an ace is an expert, someone adept

explanation.surface: A miracle cure is obtained from a skilled practitioner in an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words denote a supposed cure-all remedy.

clue.text: Reform and say nothing to closest friend

parts.note: to reform is to alter
e.g. (for example) can be replaced by 'say'
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Advice to change one's ways and keep quiet before one's best mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'other self', used of a trusted companion or bosom pal.

clue.text: Words of grave importance

parts.note: 'grave' as serious hides 'grave' as a burial place: words inscribed on a tomb

explanation.definitionFit: An inscription on a tombstone honouring the dead person.

clue.text: A padre is resolved to get there

indicators.note: resolved means sorted out, so the letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: a padre is a military chaplain

explanation.surface: A chaplain is determined to reach heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is resolved' reads as determination, but 'is' joins the fodder and 'resolved' is the anagram signal. 'there' stands for the afterlife, as in 'over there'.
explanation.definitionFit: Heaven is euphemistically the place 'over there', the final destination beyond this life.

clue.text: She saw king Edward in Virginia

indicators.note: 'in' puts the royal letters inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: VA is the postal abbreviation for Virginia
ER stands for Edwardus Rex, King Edward

explanation.surface: A woman reports catching sight of a British monarch in an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' defines a woman's name; 'saw' just links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, so a woman who could be referred to by the pronoun.

clue.text: Maybe we'll take Samuel's mentor to the holy city

parts.note: the priest Eli brought up the boy Samuel in the Old Testament
Sion is a variant spelling of Zion, Jerusalem

explanation.surface: A suggestion that a prophet's teacher be escorted to Jerusalem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' signals that the contraction of 'we will' is an example of the answer, not a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Running words together by dropping a sound, as 'we will' becomes a contraction, is an example of this.

clue.text: Submitted by the Spanish watchman

parts.note: submitted, as of an entry, means sent in
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A guard has been dispatched by Spain's authorities.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentinel is a guard or sentry keeping watch.

clue.text: Low-down English wife in Nova Scotia

indicators.note: 'in' places the two single letters inside the province abbreviation

parts.note: NS is the abbreviation for the Canadian province of Nova Scotia

explanation.surface: Gossip about an Englishman's wife living in Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: The low-down is the inside information or latest report.

clue.text: Frost wrote verse, they say

indicators.note: 'they say' signals that the word is heard, not seen

parts.note: verse is poetry, rhyme

explanation.surface: Robert Frost was a poet, as everybody knows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frost' looks like the poet Robert Frost, but it is the definition: hoar frost.
explanation.definitionFit: Rime is hoar frost, the ice crystals that form on cold surfaces.

clue.text: Scotsman squeezes a pair of Frenchmen for money

indicators.note: squeezing means holding tightly within, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: mon is a Scots dialect form of man
MM is the abbreviation of Messieurs, plural of M. for Monsieur

explanation.surface: A tight-fisted Scot puts the squeeze on two Frenchmen for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Mammon is wealth regarded as an evil influence, from the biblical personification of riches.

clue.text: Setback caused by strike

explanation.surface: A reversal of fortune brought about by industrial action.
explanation.definitionFit: A blow or reversal of fortune, and also to hit something.

clue.text: The best part of a vegetable

definitions.meaning: the innermost, choicest part, the essence
a large green gourd like an overgrown courgette

explanation.surface: Praise for the choicest portion of some produce.
explanation.definitionFit: The pith or essence of something, and also a large squash grown in British gardens.

clue.text: Grounds for changing men's diet

indicators.note: changing means altering, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Reasons for putting the menfolk on a new eating plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grounds' looks like reasons, but it means the dregs left at the bottom, as in coffee grounds; the S of 'men's' is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffee grounds are the dregs that settle at the bottom, a deposit of solid matter.

clue.text: Golf club found on western perimeter

parts.note: an edge is a boundary or perimeter

explanation.surface: A golf club is discovered lying on the western boundary of the course.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedge is a lofted iron used for short, high shots.

clue.text: Flavour enhancer for beer, whisky and game

parts.note: hops give beer its bitter flavour
Scotch is whisky made in Scotland

explanation.surface: A list of drinks and something to play, as at a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: HOPSCOTCH is a children's playground game of hopping through squares chalked on the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's playground pastime of hopping through chalked squares.
